This document contains some rough design notes about how to support transactional acknowledgements for share groups.

Application programming interface

Prior to KIP-1289, applications chose how to acknowledge record delivery using the share.acknowledgement.mode consumer configuration. It seems to me that neither implicit  nor explicit  is really ideal. I propose that we introduce a third acknowledgement mode transactional . This gives a nice clean way to enforce correct API usage in the application.

Transactional acknowledgement mode has the following features:

  • Acknowledgements are explicit, meaning that every record received from poll(Duration)  must be acknowledged using ShareConsumer.acknowledge(...)  before the next call to poll(Duration) .
  • ShareConsumer.commitSync(...)  and ShareConsumer.commitAsync(...)  are not permitted. The acknowledgements are committed as part of a transaction so these specific methods are not appropriate.
  • ShareConsumer.setAcknowledgementCommitCallback(...)  is likewise not permitted. The acknowledgements will be completed once the transaction commits so the callback is not as useful as it is with asynchronous, non-transactional acknowledgements.
  • AcknowledgeMode.RENEW  is not permitted. It is incompatible with transactions.

The following code snippet shows how the application code might look.

java producer = new KafkaProducer(prodProps); ShareConsumer shareConsumer = new KafkaShareConsumer(consumerProps) { producer.initTransactions(); producer.setShareGroupTransactionAdapter(shareConsumer); shareConsumer.subscribe(Set.of("INPUT")); ConsumerRecords recs = shareConsumer.poll(Duration.ofMillis(10000)); for (ConsumerRecord rec : recs) { producer.beginTransaction(); producer.send(new ProducerRecord("OUTPUT", 0, rec.key(), rec.value()); shareConsumer.acknowledge(rec); producer.commitTransaction(); } }]]>

We need to define some kind of bridge between the producer and the share consumer so that shareConsumer.acknowledge(rec)  results in a transactional request to be sent to the share-partition leader. This is the purpose of producer.setShareGroupTransactionAdapter() . The internal details need to be ironed out, but this gives quite clean application code (there's no Producer.sendShareGroupAcknowledgementsToTransaction()  or equivalent for example).

Kafka protocol

To fit in with the current protocol design, I think we need 2 (or perhaps 3, depending on taste) new RPCs. They are:

  • TxnShareAcknowledge - sent by the client to the share-partition leader - the transactional equivalent of ShareAcknowledge
  • TxnComplete - sent by the share coordinator to the share-partition leader at transaction completion so the record states in the share partition can be updated
  • TxnWriteShareGroupState - sent by the share-partition leader to the share coordinator - we could perhaps make these extra fields on the regular WriteShareGroupState RPC

Feature enablement

It will be necessary to introduce a new share.version  to enable this support (3). It seems that there is no need to have a new transaction.version  because there is no change to the protocol or records for the transaction coordinator. The transactions will include the __share_group_state  topic in much the way that transactions include the __consumer_offsets  topic when offsets are committed transactionally. But in both cases, the transaction coordinator is not really aware of the nuances of the behaviour of these topics, just that partitions have been registered in the transaction and transaction markers must be written at transaction completion.

TxnShareAcknowledge

Here's the request schema.

java

Note that the Gap acknowledge type is applied directly to the share partition state. Any of Accept, Release and Reject can be acknowledged transactionally. Generally Accept will be used, but a transactional application might conceivably want to release or reject as part of its transaction. The Renew acknowledge type is not supported.

ShareTxnComplete

java

TxnWriteShareGroupState

The delivery state reflects the state if the transaction commits. So, for an Accept acknowledgement, it will be Acked (2). For a release acknowledgement, it will be Available (0). For a reject acknowledgement, it will be Archiving (3) or Archived (4), depending upon whether the record will be written to the dead-letter queue.

If the transaction rolls back, the delivery state will return to Available and the delivery count will be unchanged (not decremented by the rollback).

java

ReadShareGroupState

It will be necessary to read transactional state. Here's the updated response schema.

For a transactional state, the transactional ID, producer ID and producer epoch will be provided. The delivery state will be the state if the transaction commits. If the transaction rolls back, the record will return to the Available state, and will be subject to the usual delivery count checks to determine whether it should be archived. The delivery count will be the value whether the transaction commits or rolls back.
